standard_prerequisites.name: Elements of ordinals are ordinals
standard_prerequisites.use: Line 555: transitivity of the supposed set O of all ordinals, since members of its members are ordinals.

standard_prerequisites.name: Transitive sets of ordinals are ordinals
standard_prerequisites.use: Line 556: O itself becomes an ordinal once transitive.

standard_prerequisites.name: No ordinal contains itself
standard_prerequisites.use: Line 557: O in O contradicts the irreflexivity supplied by the ordinal-ordering corollary.

core_obligations: Reductio setup (proof lines 554-555): suppose O collects all ordinals; members of members of O are ordinals, hence in O, so O is transitive.
Self-membership (line 556): a transitive set of ordinals is an ordinal, so O is an ordinal and therefore O in O.
Contradiction (line 557): O in O clashes with the corollary that ordinals are strictly ordered.
proof_roadmap: Derive transitivity from elementhood closure of ordinals.
Promote the set to an ordinal and force self-membership.
difficulty_reason: The textbook Burali-Forti paradox (statement 549-551, proof 553-559): four linked steps each resting on a named corollary of the section immediately above. H2: short, linear reductio with all three citations spelled out.
